subject: psychiatry
title: Personality Disorders: Cluster A Eccentric and Cluster B Dramatic Clusters

steps.tx: **Cluster A personality disorders** encompass paranoid, schizoid, and schizotypal personality disorders, characterized by odd, eccentric, or detached patterns of thinking and behavior. Individuals in Cluster A maintain significant biological and genetic relationships with the schizophrenia spectrum, frequently sharing familial genetic loading and cognitive deficits.
steps.say: Cluster A encompasses paranoid, schizoid, and schizotypal personalities, sharing odd eccentric behaviors and genetic links to schizophrenia.

vis.title: Cluster A Diagnostic Typology
rows: Neither desires nor enjoys close relationships; 'lone wolf'
Ideas of reference; odd beliefs; social anxiety

steps.tx: Lay the three clusters along one grid and their flavours separate quickly. Cluster A gathers the odd and withdrawn, Cluster B the dramatic and unstable, Cluster C the anxious and fearful. Reading across the rows also shows family loading, heaviest beside schizophrenia spectrum traits in Cluster A and lighter elsewhere. Keeping this **dimensional matrix** in mind stops examiners from mixing schizoid detachment with avoidant longing or antisocial disregard.
steps.say: A grid comparing the three clusters separates odd, dramatic and anxious patterns and shows where genetic loading runs heaviest.

vis.alt: Grid comparing Cluster A, Cluster B and Cluster C personality traits side by side with their differing levels of genetic loading
vis.caption: Three personality clusters arranged in one matrix, contrasting odd, dramatic and anxious traits alongside their genetic loading. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Paranoid personality disorder** features a pervasive, unjustified distrust and suspiciousness of others such that their motives are interpreted as malevolent, beginning by early adulthood. Sufferers suspect without basis that others are exploiting or deceiving them, read hidden threatening meanings into benign remarks, and bear unrelenting grudges.
steps.say: Paranoid personality disorder involves pervasive suspiciousness, reading hidden malevolent meanings into innocent remarks, and bearing bitter grudges.

left.title: Paranoid Personality
points: Non-delusional, pervasive suspiciousness
Expects trickery and deception from colleagues
Pathologically jealous regarding marital partner
Overly sensitive to perceived slights

right.title: Delusional Disorder
points: Fixed, unshakeable systematized delusions
Circumscribed to a specific persecutory theme
Later onset in mid-to-late adulthood
Higher intensity and loss of reality testing

steps.tx: **Schizoid personality disorder** is characterized by a pervasive pattern of detachment from social relationships and a restricted range of emotional expression in interpersonal settings. Patients neither desire nor enjoy close personal relationships, almost always choose solitary activities, display indifference to praise or criticism, and exhibit emotional coldness.
steps.say: Schizoid individuals are true loners who neither desire nor enjoy social relationships, preferring solitary activities and showing emotional detachment.

left.title: Schizoid Personality
points: Zero internal desire for social relationships
Completely content with lifelong isolation
Indifferent to approval or critical remarks
Prefers abstract solitary intellectual tasks

right.title: Avoidant Personality
points: Intensely yearns for social connection
Isolated due to terror of rejection and shame
Extremely sensitive to negative evaluation
Suffers profound loneliness and distress

steps.tx: **Schizotypal personality disorder** is characterized by acute discomfort with close relationships, cognitive or perceptual distortions, and eccentric behavior. Hallmark features include ideas of reference (incorrect interpretations of casual incidents as having personal meaning), magical thinking, superstitious beliefs, odd metaphorical speech, and paranoid ideation.
steps.say: Schizotypal personality presents with magical thinking, ideas of reference, eccentric speech, and odd behavior, genetically tied to schizophrenia.

vis.title: Schizotypal Features
rows: Held with less rigidity than frank delusions
Lacks gross schizophrenic incoherence or neologisms
Social anxiety tied to paranoid mistrust
Does not diminish with familiarity or reassurance

steps.tx: **Cluster B personality disorders** encompass antisocial, borderline, histrionic, and narcissistic personality disorders, marked by dramatic, emotional, erratic, or impulsive behaviors. These disorders carry high rates of substance use disorders, mood instability, forensic criminality, and turbulent interpersonal relationships that repeatedly disrupt social functioning.
steps.say: Cluster B includes antisocial, borderline, histrionic, and narcissistic disorders, characterized by dramatic, erratic, and impulsive behaviors.

vis.title: Cluster B Dramatic Spectrum
rows: Disregard for laws and rights of others
Lack of remorse; requires conduct disorder <15y
Affective instability and fear of abandonment
Grandiosity, entitlement, and lack of empathy

steps.tx: **Antisocial personality disorder** is defined by a pervasive pattern of disregard for and violation of the rights of others occurring since age 15. Key criteria include repeated criminal acts, deceitfulness, impulsivity, physical aggressiveness, reckless disregard for safety, consistent irresponsibility, and complete absence of remorse.
steps.say: Antisocial personality requires a history of conduct disorder before age fifteen, manifesting with lawbreaking, deceit, aggression, and lack of remorse.

left.title: Diagnostic Mandates
points: Current age at least eighteen years
Evidence of conduct disorder onset before age 15
Repeated unlawful acts warranting arrest
Total absence of guilt or moral remorse

right.title: Clinical Phenotype
points: Pathological lying and conning others for profit
Irritable aggression and recurrent physical fights
Reckless disregard for safety of self or others
Chronic failure to sustain financial obligations

steps.tx: **Borderline personality disorder** features pervasive instability of interpersonal relationships, self-image, and affects, alongside marked impulsivity beginning in early adulthood. Sufferers make frantic efforts to avoid real or imagined abandonment, demonstrate identity disturbance, experience chronic feelings of emptiness, and engage in recurrent suicidal gestures.
steps.say: Borderline personality involves severe emotional instability, fear of abandonment, chronic emptiness, and recurrent self-harm gestures.

nodes.label: Perceived threat of abandonment or delayed reply
Primitive splitting: idealization abruptly flips to intense devaluation
Intense affective rage, panic, and chronic emptiness
Impulsive self-harm or suicidal gesture to regulate distress

steps.tx: **Histrionic personality disorder** involves a pervasive pattern of excessive emotionality and attention seeking, presenting with discomfort when not the center of attention. Patients interact through inappropriate sexually seductive behavior, display rapidly shifting and shallow emotions, utilize physical appearance to draw focus, and speak in an impressionistic style.
steps.say: Histrionic personality features theatrical attention seeking, sexually seductive interactions, shallow shifting emotions, and exaggerated speech.

left.title: Histrionic Traits
points: Uncomfortable when not the center of attention
Inappropriately provocative and seductive
Dramatic theatricality with exaggerated emotions
Considers relationships more intimate than they are

right.title: Borderline Contrasted
points: Profound self-harm and suicidal behavior
Chronic inner emptiness and identity diffusion
Transient stress-related paranoid ideation
Severe micro-psychotic dissociative episodes
